description: Formal capability catalog for perry-wit AOT TypeScript compiler targeting WASI Preview 2

tiers.name: Tier 1: Web Standard Primaries
tiers.description: Universal web and ECMAScript primitives available without environment-specific imports

tiers.name: Tier 2: Node Core Builtins
tiers.description: Node.js platform primitives mapped to WASI Preview 2 host capabilities

tiers.name: Non-Goals
tiers.description: Features explicitly excluded from AOT WebAssembly compilation

capabilities.name: Object Spread Operator
capabilities.domain: Shallow object property merging ({ ...a, ...b }) with right-to-left property override semantics
invariants: Evaluates object operands left-to-right
Produces a new distinct object identity
Overwrites keys present in earlier objects with keys from later objects
Preserves string, numeric, boolean, array, and nested object property values
differences: Executed natively via guest runtime handle table and NaN-boxing rather than prototype lookups

capabilities.name: Console Stream Routing
capabilities.domain: Writing formatted text to standard I/O streams
invariants: console.log writes UTF-8 text to WASI stdout descriptor with a trailing newline
console.error writes UTF-8 text to WASI stderr descriptor with a trailing newline
Writes are immediately flushed to the host stream
differences: Supports string primitives directly; object inspection formats via JSON representation

capabilities.name: Promise.all Concurrency
capabilities.domain: Concurrent dispatch and collection of multiple asynchronous operations
invariants: Dispatches all operand promises concurrently without sequential blocking
Resolves with an array of resolved values preserving the original input order
Fails fast upon the first rejected promise
differences: Cooperative polling on WASIp2 event loop via wasi:io/poll rather than a JS microtask queue

capabilities.name: global.fetch
capabilities.domain: Asynchronous HTTP network requests using wasi:http/outgoing-handler
invariants: Dispatches HTTP GET and POST requests to valid absolute URLs
Returns a Promise resolving to a Response handle
Rejects on connection refusal, DNS failure, or network timeout without crashing host
differences: Does not support loopback redirects, custom CA stores, or WebSocket upgrades

capabilities.name: Response.prototype.json
capabilities.domain: Consuming HTTP response body stream and parsing UTF-8 JSON into typed structures
invariants: Streams incoming body chunks from wasi:http input-stream
Parses valid JSON objects, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans
Rejects the returned Promise with a SyntaxError when body is malformed JSON
differences: Parsed structures are held in guest runtime handles and can be directly splatted or serialized

capabilities.name: process.exit
capabilities.domain: Process termination with an explicit numeric exit code
invariants: Immediately halts execution and propagates code to wasi:cli/exit@0.2.x
Code 0 denotes success; non-zero codes denote failure
differences: Does not invoke Node beforeExit or exit listener hooks

capabilities.name: performance.now and Monotonic Clocks
capabilities.domain: High-resolution monotonic time measurement using wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock
invariants: performance.now() returns monotonic time in milliseconds as a float
Values never decrease across successive calls
differences: Resolution and origin are backed by the host's wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock implementation

capabilities.name: Date and Wall Clocks
capabilities.domain: Wall clock time and date calendar operations using wasi:clocks/wall-clock
invariants: Date.now() returns current UTC timestamp in milliseconds since UNIX epoch
new Date(timestamp) and new Date() instantiate valid Date objects
getTime(), toISOString(), and calendar getters (getFullYear, getMonth, getDate, getDay, getHours, getMinutes, getSeconds, getMilliseconds) operate in UTC
differences: Backed by wasi:clocks/wall-clock; parsing arbitrary human-formatted date strings is currently deferred

capabilities.name: Randomness and Cryptography
capabilities.domain: Cryptographic and pseudo-random generation using wasi:random
invariants: Math.random() generates floating point numbers in [0.0, 1.0)
crypto.randomUUID() generates valid RFC 4122 v4 UUID strings
crypto.getRandomValues(arr) fills typed arrays in-place with secure random bytes and returns the array instance
differences: Powered by wasi:random/random and wasi:random/insecure interfaces

capabilities.name: Dynamic Code Evaluation (eval / new Function)
capabilities.domain: Runtime evaluation of dynamic JavaScript strings
differences: Incompatible with AOT compilation directly to WebAssembly bytecode without embedded interpreter

capabilities.name: Child Process Spawning
capabilities.domain: Spawning arbitrary OS processes via fork / exec
differences: WASI Preview 2 does not permit unconstrained host process spawning inside the sandbox
